clue.text: Capital clown's not coming back

parts.note: Launce is the clown (comic servant) in Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona, here with a possessive S

indicators.note: coming back means the little word before it is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jester is staying put rather than returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns NOT into TON. LAUNCESTON was the ancient capital (county town) of Cornwall, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Launceston was historically the county town of Cornwall, its old capital until the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Survive without eating? It's not recorded

definitions.meaning: jokingly, to subsist on nothing but the atmosphere
describing a broadcast going out live rather than prerecorded

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to subsist on nothing and to be broadcast as it happens.

clue.text: In desert land, lion has no stomach for parts of limb

indicators.note: In means the shortened lion goes inside the desert country

parts.note: UAE is the United Arab Emirates, a desert country

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle, so the middle letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lion in the desert has no appetite for its prey's limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no stomach' means losing the middle letters; the lion's prey and limbs in the surface are a picture only.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones; this is its plural.

clue.text: In the glasshouse, they play ball

definitions.meaning: the great glass and iron exhibition hall of 1851 in London
the London football club named after it

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both the Victorian glass exhibition building and the football club named after it.

clue.text: Bore to extremes, and glaze over — still here?

indicators.note: over means the glaze word sits over, around, the next piece

parts.note: a glaze gives a sheen, a glossy surface

indicators.note: to extremes means only the first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A tedious person whose eyes glaze over, asking if anyone is still around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to extremes' takes B and E from Bore; 'over' puts SHEEN around them. 'still' is not 'yet' but an illicit distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, an Irish word, where illicitly distilled liquor might be made.

clue.text: Leave car here perhaps getting shot

definitions.meaning: you might park a car on the driveway
a cricket stroke played to the leg side

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a place to park at home and a stroke in cricket, a British bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Consort embraces new coquette

indicators.note: embraces means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to consort with people is to mix with them

explanation.surface: A royal spouse hugs a flirtatious newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette and a minx are both pert, flirtatious young women; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: New leader for powerful women creates favourable effect

indicators.note: a new first letter replaces the current one

parts.note: empresses are female rulers

explanation.surface: Fresh leadership for strong women makes a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New leader for' swaps the first letter E of EMPRESSES for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to make a favourable impact on someone.

clue.text: Unknown nobody rises to be member of nobility?

parts.note: X is the mathematician's unknown quantity

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: none means no one

explanation.surface: An obscure commoner ascends to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns NONE into ENON. The nobility here are the noble gases.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is one of the noble gases, so a member of that chemical family.

clue.text: In front, ditch collar

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession
a dyke is a ditch or drainage channel

explanation.surface: Someone digging a trench at the front of a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vandyke is a wide lace collar with pointed edges, as painted by Van Dyck.

clue.text: Brush with this stand-up comic

parts.note: read as a comedian you have a run-in with, it is really the household item partnered with a brush, standing up when stored

explanation.surface: Having a scrape with a stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the household companion you sweep dirt into with a brush.

clue.text: Down under, see it up over

definitions.text: Down under, see it up over

parts.words: Down under, see it up over
parts.note: in Australia, look overhead at night and this constellation is visible

explanation.surface: A playful twist on Down Under, with things seen up above.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southern Cross is a constellation seen in the southern hemisphere skies, featured on Australia's flag.

clue.text: Not locked away, but one's done time

parts.note: something done and finished is over

explanation.surface: A released prisoner who has served a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison picture of 'locked away' and 'done time' hides a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and unconcealed, the opposite of shut away or hidden.

clue.text: Poem written to vase, holding each one sensuous and Greek

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem

indicators.note: holding means the vase word contains the next piece

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Verses addressed to a Greek vase by a pleasure-loving poet, in the manner of Keats.
explanation.definitionFit: An Epicurean follows the Greek philosopher Epicurus and, loosely, is a person devoted to sensual pleasure.

clue.text: Shyster drawn by the siren's call?

definitions.text: Shyster drawn by the siren's call?

parts.words: Shyster drawn by the siren's call?
parts.note: a crooked lawyer lured not by a mythical singer but by an emergency vehicle's wail, chasing accident victims for business

explanation.surface: A disreputable lawyer lured like a sailor by a seductive siren.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who pursues accident victims for compensation cases is derided by this phrase.

clue.text: What may make service book — one feature article

parts.note: taken as written
the chin is a facial feature
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A book with one featured article in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner or tea service, a set of tableware, may be made of fine porcelain of this kind.

clue.text: Creating new image, try single change

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Advice to try a different single to revamp a pop image.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyling is giving something a new look or style, such as a haircut or brand.

clue.text: Agonising errors in transcribing rhyme

indicators.note: making errors while transcribing jumbles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A copyist laments the painful mistakes made in writing out a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in transcribing' signals that the letters of AGONISING ERRORS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional English nursery rhyme sung while children dance in a circle.

clue.text: Furious consumer's heard to deny wearing mink?

indicators.note: heard tells you the words are said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: to deny wearing mink is to say IN FUR? NO

explanation.surface: An animal-rights protester shouts in rage at a fur wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals a sound-alike: 'in fur? no' spoken. The furious consumer is a raging fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A raging fire that consumes everything is a blaze of this kind.

clue.text: Loved the stage, in which I rose as actor

indicators.note: in a down clue, rose means the whole sequence is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: dug, from dig, is slang for liked or loved

indicators.note: in which means the next letter goes inside the stage word

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or contest

explanation.surface: A thespian who adored the theatre and rose to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the stage' suggests theatre, but it is a leg of a race; 'rose' reverses the whole run in this down clue. John Gielgud was a great English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Gielgud was one of the leading English stage and screen actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Meal thus repeating on driver with a couple to drop off?

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.text: with a couple to drop off
indicators.note: a couple of letters, the final two, fall away from the end of the driver word

parts.note: a chauffeur is a hired driver

explanation.surface: A chauffeur's passengers get out while a meal repeats on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a couple to drop off' removes UR from CHAUFFEUR, leaving CHAUFFE. The surface plays on passengers being dropped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A réchauffé is a dish of warmed-up leftovers, food served a second time.

clue.text: One avoided going north, having to drive back

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a leper was traditionally shunned and avoided

explanation.surface: Someone shunned travels north, having to drive back.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to drive them back.

clue.text: Crowing arrogantly?

parts.note: boasting in a conceited manner, with a nod to the farmyard bird that crows

explanation.surface: Someone gloating with self-satisfied swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky means conceited and overconfident, behaviour likened to a strutting cockerel.

clue.text: Desert features some heroic activity

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Brave deeds on display in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are the typical plants of deserts, so features of a desert landscape.

clue.text: Early season almost perfect, but frost is penetrating

indicators.note: is penetrating means the frost word goes inside the other piece
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: pure can mean perfect or unblemished
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Spring is nearly ideal, but a frost is getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the perfect word before the frost goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeur is French for the first produce of the season, early fruit, vegetables or new wine.

clue.text: Dough, a grand prisoner returned — not entirely smart

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: returned means the prisoner word is read backwards

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart

explanation.surface: A thousand-pound sum handed back by a stylish convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like money after 'grand', but it is the pasta dumpling; 'returned' and 'not entirely' each act only on the word beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made of dough, usually potato and flour.

clue.text: Weight boy carries round

indicators.note: carries means the boy word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A boy hauling something round.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is a burden or weight that is carried.

clue.text: Sharing work space in shed, ink got spilled

indicators.note: spilled ink is scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ink was knocked over in a garden shed office.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-desking is the office practice of workers using whichever desk is free rather than their own.
